name: Alex's Reader
subtitle: One app, kept fresh.
description: The private build of Reader, published for the people it was made for.

apps.name: Reader
apps.subtitle: Books, catalogs, and volume-key page turns.
apps.localizedDescription: A personal e-book reader. Reads EPUB, FB2, MOBI, AZW3 and CBZ, pulls books from any OPDS catalog, and turns pages with a swipe, a tap or the hardware volume keys. The page is set like a printed one: a running head, a text block and a folio, in six themes.

versions.localizedDescription:
Your reading now sits on the Home Screen. Add the Reader widget and your run of days, today's reading and how much of your daily goal is behind you are there without opening anything.
Three sizes: the smallest holds the streak and today, the largest adds this week and the book you are part-way through — tap that one to carry straight on reading.
The widget takes whichever reading theme you use, and is written in your own language.

Arrange your books onto shelves you name yourself — hold a book to lift it and drag it onto one, and a book can sit on as many shelves as you like.
Send a book to somebody, or save it into Files and so to iCloud Drive, from the book's own menu.
Marking a book read now asks when you finished it, so the ones you read years ago land on the right day rather than today. You can change the date later from the book's page.
A book's reading figures are one tap from the shelf, the type settings can be put back the way they came, and today's total fits inside the goal circle again in Ukrainian and Russian.

A new Stats tab counts your reading: how long, on which days, how fast, and how many days in a row you have kept it up.
Every book gets a page of that too, down to how much longer it will take at the pace you actually read.
Save your whole library — books, bookmarks and where you are in each one — into a single file you can keep in iCloud Drive, then put it back on any phone.
The app now speaks Ukrainian and Russian as well as English, following your phone unless you choose for yourself in Settings.

Bookmark the page you are on with the ribbon at the top, and get back to it from the contents.
Choose how a page turns — it can slide, lift off the top, or lay the next page over it.
Scrolling instead of pages now really scrolls: drag the text with your finger and it carries on when you let go.
Fixed a theme change leaving the old colour around the edges of the page, and a picker that offered nothing but ZIP files.

Tap a picture in a book to open it full screen — pinch or double-tap for a closer look.
Tap the small number beside a word to read its note, and the button in the corner brings you back to the page you were on.

A proper app icon — a walnut page, instead of the blue placeholder.
Nothing else in the app has changed.

The first build: your own shelf, the catalogs you pull books from, and a page set like a printed one — running head, text block, page number.
Page numbers stopped drifting when you crossed into a new chapter, the controls no longer swallow a page turn, and the shelf finds Cyrillic titles.
